status.summary: Active, coming off a loss. Quillan Salkilld submitted him with a rear-naked choke at 4:25 of round 1 in a UFC Fight Night main event in Las Vegas (Aug 8, 2026). Before that he submitted Esteban Ribovics with an arm-triangle at UFC 327 (Apr 11, 2026), and in Oct 2025 Charles Oliveira choked him out in Rio. He is 2-2 in his last four. UFC record 9-5 in fighters.json. No booking, current ranking or injury could be confirmed: web search was unavailable to the research pass and to the Nov 6, 2026 fact-check, and none of the project's other research files lists one. The Salkilld, Ribovics and Oliveira results were re-checked against fighters.json, the raw bout stats and the Salkilld and Oliveira dossiers' recap accounts.

arm-triangle from half guard (finished Esteban Ribovics, UFC 327) and kimura from side control (finished Jeremy Stephens, 2021)
knees to the body on the ground (TKO of Diego Ferreira, 2021)

weaknesses: back exposure in scrambles: rear-naked choke losses to Charles Oliveira (R2, Oct 2025) and Quillan Salkilld (R1, Aug 2026)

gets dropped: 5 knockdowns absorbed in 159.5 UFC minutes (0.47 per 15 min vs a median of about 0.24), though never stopped by strikes
takedown accuracy only 38%: Beneil Dariush stopped 15 of his 19 attempts (UFC 280)
his takedown defence has slipped to 53% recency-weighted (77% career): Oliveira and Salkilld each scored their one takedown
style.summary: A wrestler who wins on takedown volume. He shoots almost four times as often as the median lightweight, holds top position for about a third of his fight time, and finishes with ground strikes or chokes from top. Standing, he lands little but is hard to hit cleanly. His recent losses came against elite grapplers who took his back in scrambles.

moves.notes: Group weights (head, body, leg) each sum to 1. The engine's target split should come from fighters.json: recency-weighted landed shares are head 0.80 / body 0.13 / leg 0.07 and attempt shares are head 0.87 / body 0.09 / leg 0.04 (career landed 0.77 / 0.14 / 0.10). About a quarter of his recent landed strikes are ground strikes, which these standing weights do not cover. No published punch-by-punch breakdown could be fetched in this pass, so the head group is a generic straight-punch-first spread (with his southpaw listing the 'cross' is the rear left hand), with overhands, uppercuts and head kicks minor. UFC Stats does not split body or leg strikes into punches and kicks, so body weights are near even and calf/inside are split evenly. His landed leg strikes are few (5 of 5 vs Klein, 9 of 9 vs Turner, 14 of 15 vs Holtzman). Spinning is 0: none of his finishes used one. Knee is 0.15 for the ground-knee TKO of Ferreira; elbow is 0.05. These weights are analyst judgment from the bout stats above.

engine_notes.note: Takedown volume is the core skill: 13.3 attempts per 15 min career at 38% (5.1 landed per 15; lightweight medians about 3.6 attempted and 1.2 landed), 11.8 attempts at 42% recency-weighted.
Top-control share: 285 control seconds per 15 min career and 332 recency-weighted (32-37% of fight time; median about 17%). Opponents control him only 7-10% of the time.

Knocked down 5 times in 159.5 minutes (Kutateladze, Tsarukyan, Dariush, Turner, Dos Anjos; 0.47 per 15) but 0 KO/TKO losses in 14 UFC fights, so knockdowns should not convert into finishes at the usual rate.
Submission risk comes from scrambles rather than off his back: both submission losses were rear-naked chokes after the opponent took his back (Oliveira R2 2:48, Salkilld R1 4:25).

Five-round pace evidence is thin: the pace curve (1.00 / 2.45 / 2.68 / 1.74 / 2.68) shows output rising after round 1, but rounds 3-5 rest on one fight (Tsarukyan, 2022). Treat late-round claims as uncertain.
